newsitem.title: UK: Next UK monetary meetings due May 7, June 5.
newsitem.headline: Next UK monetary meetings due May 7, June 5.

text.p: The next monetary meetings between the Chancellor of the Exchequer and Bank of England Governor Eddie George have been provisionally scheduled for May 7 and June 5, the Treasury said.
If confirmed, the May 7 meeting would be the first after the May 1 election.
Opinion polls suggest the opposition Labour party is likely to oust the ruling Conservatives, which means George would meet Labour's Gordon Brown rather than Kenneth Clarke.
Labour has pledged to reform the monetary policy framework if it takes office, establishing a monetary policy committee at the Bank and a council of economic advisers at the Treasury.
Minutes of the last monetary meeting on April 10 will be published on May 21 at 0830 GMT. Interest rates were left unchanged at 6.0 percent after that meeting.
